title: Reuters' parent company to launch Thomson 1.1 by year-end: Zhipu GLM and Google Gemma selected as foundation models, with focus on computer operation capabilities

content_html:
Thomson Reuters plans to keep using open source to hold down its AI costs. According to Business Insider, the Reuters parent company will launch a new model, Thomson 1.1, by the end of this year. Its base models are open-source models that anyone can download and deploy themselves—GLM from China's Zhipu AI and Google's Gemma. The company hopes this will reduce AI costs while giving it better control over its intellectual property.

Two Generations of In-House Models in a Row, Both Based on Chinese Base Models

For Thomson Reuters, adopting a Google model marks a shift: when it developed its previous in-house model, Thomson 1.0, it did not use a U.S. AI model; instead, it built its own chatbot on Qwen from Chinese tech giant Alibaba. In other words, for two consecutive generations of in-house models, the base models have come from China's open-source camp.

GLM for Operations, Gemma for Efficiency

CTO Joel Hron explained the selection rationale: the company still uses Zhipu's GLM because it excels at computer use—a key capability for AI agents; it chose Gemma for its small size and high efficiency. In terms of positioning, this model targets moderately complex client work, such as tax consulting; for the most complex tasks, the company still plans to leave those to models from OpenAI and Anthropic. With open source as the foundation and closed source as the backstop, it balances cost and capability.
